Definition: from G1223 and σαφής (clear); to clear thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) declare:--tell unto.
BiblicalUsage: To explain plainly is to make a thing clear, and the word stands twice in Matthew. The disciples ask Jesus to declare the parable of the tares, and the servants come to their lord and declare plainly all that was done to his fellow servant.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that plain explaining is a mercy; Jesus does not leave His disciples guessing at the parable, and the servant who declares the whole matter plainly is the one the master hears.
